text:
anya: heads up — spotted an odd NDCG drop after bringing up redwood-rank-compact-v2 int4 in shadowbench this morning. ndcg@10 down ~1.8%, mrr@1 down ~0.6%.

sam: which slice? longdocs/shortqueries/geo?

anya: primarily longdocs (>=800 tokens). short queries unaffected. also seems worse for docs with HTML-ish titles (unicode punctuation).

ravi: was this immediately post-PTQ quant step or after model swap + infra change?

anya: model swap + PTQ. we landed the hybrid int4 config and tested locally — small models looked fine. production shadowbench replicates the delta.

jen: any difference in candidate pools between baseline vs compact-v2 runs? ordering, shuffling, dedupe?

anya: we used same candidate ids and same sampling seed. confirmed with a quick diff of candidate sets. ordering preserved.

ravi: could be serialization / tokenization mismatch at eval-time vs offline. did we preprocess through the same tokenizer/normalizer?

anya: good call. I grabbed a couple failing cases and compared tokenization. found that some doc titles include a ZERO-WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (U+FEFF) from HTML sanitization on ingest — baseline model eval pipeline strips it; the new bringup pipeline (minor library bump) doesn't. That changes token boundaries for a subset.

sam: interesting. that could change kv-cache alignment or attention state leading to slight rerank score shifts. how many examples affected?

anya: ~2.3% of longdocs had the character. but the ndcg drop concentrated on tail cohorts where those docs are top-3 candidate.

jen: still, a 1.8% ndcg hit seems bigger. any evidence of quant-specific amplification (int4 sensitivity) of those token-boundary changes?

ravi: yes — int4 tends to amplify small embedding/logit shifts in rankers due to reduced dynamic range. If tokenization change moves tokenization over a subtoken boundary, embeddings can differ more after quantization. We saw similar in a different bringup (smallscale) — small token shift -> larger score delta under int4.

anya: to reproduce locally I ran:

```
# reproduce failing case
python eval_rerank.py --model redwood-rank-compact-v2 --quant int4 --candidates-file sample.json 
  --tokenizer-version v2 --strip-bom true
```

When I toggle `--strip-bom false` the ndcg gap widens; with `--strip-bom true` we get parity with baseline.

sam: nice repro. next steps? we can either fix preprocessing parity across pipelines or apply a conservative post-token normalization in the bringup. Also important to check whether prefix-caching or kvpack changes amplify this.

anya: I tried disabling prefix cache in shadowbench and reran — ndcg gap shrank by ~0.4 percentage points but didn't disappear. So both effects combine.

jen: action items: 1) enforce BOM/ZWNB removal in bringup eval pipeline and prod ingest normalization (assign to @ravi), 2) run an int4 sensitivity sweep on token-boundary-perturbed docs (assign to @anya), 3) validate prefix-cache interaction with quantized models (assign to @sam), 4) consider adding a small pre-rollout quality gate that checks tokenization parity across ingest+eval.

ravi: taking 1). I'll add a normalization step to the bringup pipeline and push a tiny patch.

deploy-bot: canary patch pushed to redwood-infra/proc-normalize-token (sha: 7f3b2a) — running CI. :rocket:

anya: thanks. I'll run the int4 sensitivity sweep once the patch lands. I'll also produce a short doc with failing example ids and token diffs.

ops-bot: note — logging ticket created #INF-8342 for normalization parity and #ML-5821 for int4 sensitivity sweep.

sam: one more thing — let's add a small eval that compares ndcg when you intentionally insert/remove zero-width chars to quantify amplification. might be a helpful unit in the bringup checklist.

anya: agreed. I'll add that to the checklist and post results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
